correctness.rationale: For each \(n\ge3\), the two marginals are \(1/n\). When a fixed-point site touches the chosen succession edge, both images are prescribed, giving joint probability \(1/[n(n-1)]\). Otherwise conditioning on a fixed value leaves \((n-1)(n-2)\) ordered image pairs, exactly \(n-1-c_j\) of which are consecutive, where \(c_j\) is one at an endpoint and two in the interior. Subtraction proves every matrix entry. Scaling the matrix and inspecting its first and interior columns yields the complete alternating left kernel, proving the even/odd rank. Row and column sums yield all aggregate identities; \(n=2\) is handled directly. Actual standalone code independently exhausts \(n=2\) to \(8\) and checks matrix rank to \(40\). No unproved infinite inference comes from computation.

value.rationale: The known equality in distribution of two shuffle-diagnostic point processes naturally motivates measuring their *same-sample* dependence. The theorem fully resolves an indexed covariance-sign classification with positive boundary/incidence but negative interior entries and shows a sharp rank loss exactly for odd \(n\), equivalent to an uncorrelated alternating succession mode. The rank classification is not a marginal-law corollary; the boundary-dominated aggregate dependence and parity-null mode are structurally informative for linear prediction and null diagnostics. No downstream general theorem is claimed.
